claim: CAS is opt-in per disk through `metadata_type = content_addressed` and coexists with zero-copy replication rather than replacing it.

CAS design changes are gated by adversarial review, green TLA+ safety and liveness stages with negative controls, deterministic chaos soak checks, and deterministic gtests; a negative control that does not reproduce its named counterexample is treated as a failed gate.

CAS mechanisms are rejected when they require Keeper for correctness, scale Keeper or S3 work with data volume, let a stuck writer stall pool-wide reclamation, can accelerate deletion past safety gates, or couple generic `ReplicatedMergeTree` surfaces to the CA disk implementation.

Blob identity uses an in-body incarnation tag and an exact backend token for deletion; generations are absent from object keys, so the `404 → LIST` degraded read path is unnecessary and Keeper is optional.

Blob in-degree is derived from a folded set of source-edge deltas keyed by `(kind, hash, source_manifest)` rather than stored as a mutable counter; set semantics can delay reclamation but cannot accelerate deletion.
Immutable CAS content uses a binary hashed format and mutable hot-path objects use protobuf; JSON, pack objects, and the write-only build-heartbeat object were removed from the format design.
Garage was rejected as a CAS backend because it silently ignores conditional operations such as `If-None-Match`, while RustFS passed the conditional-write battery.
Issue `B140` was caused by `reuseBlob` transferring a blob hash without transferring its `cas_owner` protection, allowing GC to delete a blob still referenced by a committed part.
Build-root reachability and fail-closed commit are both required to prevent the `B140` dangle; either mechanism alone still has a counterexample.
A lazy closure read of an absent tree must not record an empty closure; precommit must record the closure structure so the referenced blob cannot leak forever.
The intermediate `B167` blob-watermark design had a livelock in which GC could re-condemn a build's fresh upload during the non-atomic upload-to-publish gap, preventing publication forever.
The build watermark `build_seq` must be monotone; a non-monotone sequence can move `min_active` backward and re-protect a condemned blob, causing a leak.

GC uses a hot `cas/refs/` path for listed reference metadata and a cold `cas/manifests/` path for cursor-paged manifest bodies; discovery is `GET gc/state + LIST cas/refs/` with cost proportional to reference shards.

Namespace discovery does not use a persistent `gc/registry`; each namespace has a durable monotone never-reused `incarnation`, and the pool has a global GC `round`, because both coordinates are required to prevent newborn and ABA errors.

The ack-floor GC round replaces fence and recheck phases with a three-cursor streaming merge and one `gc/state` CAS; graduation requires `condemn_round < min_ack` and two-phase `delete_pending` handling.
A GC fold that holds back a landed reference must declare the hold; a silent hold-back is unsafe because it can produce the `31 dangling blobs` counterexample.
All decision-bearing GC artifacts, including `retired` and `outcomes`, are under `gc/gen/<g>/attempt/<a>/`, and only the adopted attempt is reader-visible.
Refs use a writer-owned immutable snapshot plus an append-only log with strictly increasing ids, and a per-table `CasSingleWriterSlot` makes intra-server append conflicts structurally impossible.
A sealed ref snapshot carries its own fold cursor, and the ref log may be trimmed only through that cursor.
The `EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE` order is precommit with durable closure, then adopt/observe, then promote; under this order promote-time revalidation of tokened leaves is redundant.
Freshness metadata is advisory: writers may point-read per-hash `.meta`, but reads do not consult it, GC deletes the blob body first, and an absent meta is equivalent to `Clean`.

Per-incarnation body keys such as `blobs/xx/<hash>.<incarnation>` were rejected because they recreate the generation-in-key race, force `404 → LIST`, and leak incarnation into pure-content manifest identity.

The resurrect-reupload orphan occurred when exact-token deletion skipped a newer token and a touch-gated hash-keyed fold never re-condemned that replacement token; the fix made `closeBlob` re-condemn the current token.
An asynchronous condemn-marker write failure must not be swallowed: graduation to `delete_pending` requires confirmed durable `Condemned` evidence, otherwise the entry carries to a later round.
Mount lease handover uses rev.6 lease-boundary exclusivity: an unclean handover waits, a clean release is fast, and a successor commits an eager recovery-snapshot seal before it becomes writable.
The mount write-fence deadline uses `CLOCK_BOOTTIME`, and expired-mount reclaim requires observing a stable holder token for a full `TTL + Drift` window on the reclaimer's own monotonic clock.
An acknowledged-then-lost `INSERT` was fixed by closing the disk transaction in `renameParts`, making the part durable before the Keeper commit that acknowledges it.

The `TXN-ONE-PIPELINE` design gives `IDiskTransaction::precommit` an explicit two-phase contract: CA precommit performs manifest publish through promote, CA commit materializes durable intent, and one `dispatch` funnel replaces the CA subclass.
All part files, including previously mutable files, are content-addressed; committed-part repoint and an MVCC atomic-write short-circuit handle updates.

A reference-only `FREEZE` was rejected because `shadow/` is contractually filesystem-readable through hardlinks for external backup pipelines; the backup design instead uses snapshot, mirror, fetch, and restore verbs.

The wide-insert baseline improved from 58.41 seconds to 30.26 seconds and from 3.0x to 1.59x versus plain S3 after `CasBlobUploadPool` and `fanOutBlobUploads`; top-thread share fell from 72.3% to 14.5%.
The GC round-duration study measured 0.465–0.535 ms per total S3 request, making a 30-minute round equivalent to 3.42 million serial round trips; 39.6% were redundant manifest refetches.

An orphan-manifest sweep premise that `unowned` implies no folded edges is false: a precommit's `+1` edges can already be folded, so deleting the manifest body leaves folded edges permanently stranded.
A RustFS ref-log enumeration omitted durable predecessor keys `0x1430c` and `0x1430d` while returning later `0x1430e`; exact-key `GET` and `HEAD` still reported the omitted objects present.

Paginated LIST cannot authorize destructive CAS decisions: a contract-compliant store may omit writes concurrent with an enumeration, but exact-key reads and conditional writes are trusted; LIST may only delay work.

Ref-log ids are dense `1..T` within `(namespace, epoch)`, derived from the table's `greatest_applied`; an id can be reused only when no attempt was sent or every sent attempt has conclusive rejection.
The in-band epoch seal occupies the exact log key that a dying predecessor would use, making conditional create the handover fence without a grace interval.

The per-life `_ckpt` object carries `committed_through`, the exact acknowledged frontier, plus the checkpoint-snapshot pointer and seal chain; append order is log PUT, `_ckpt` CAS, then acknowledgement.
The namespace catalog is a token-CAS universe read as a cut; opaque 128-bit life ids in every key make removed-life debris inert and avoid physical-emptiness proofs for removal.

Production destruction was suppressed in Stage A because pool-wide blob in-degree could contain an acknowledged `+1` from an invisible namespace while a visible `-1` was folded; suppression may be lifted only after the namespace universe is authoritative.

Recovery is authority-based: catalog cut, exact `_ckpt`, validated snapshot triple, and finite arithmetic replay ending exactly at `committed_through`; it does not use a stream LIST as a recovery hint.
A `Live` or `Removing` namespace row requires a readable `_ckpt` carrying `life_epoch`; only `Creating` is exempt during the publish-before-flip window.
Namespace creation publishes the `_ckpt` with `life_epoch` before flipping the catalog row to `Live`, while the janitor deletes `_ckpt` only when `catalog_cut.life_index.resolve(*life_id)` is false.
Global jemalloc profiling is enabled with `<jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>1</jemalloc_enable_global_profiler>` in server XML and requires a server restart; sampling begins at boot.
On ClickHouse 26.x, `SYSTEM JEMALLOC ENABLE PROFILE` can leave `prof.active` equal to `1` while producing dumps with zero stacks; a dump must contain `@ 0x` stack lines before the session is trusted.
Per-query jemalloc profiling uses `jemalloc_enable_profiler = 1`; `jemalloc_collect_profile_samples_in_trace_log = 1` additionally records per-query `JemallocSample` rows in `system.trace_log`.

The symbolized jemalloc SQL dump is `SELECT line FROM system.jemalloc_profile_text SETTINGS jemalloc_profile_text_output_format = 'symbolized', jemalloc_profile_text_symbolize_with_inline = 1 FORMAT TSVRaw`; symbolized output needs no binary for `jeprof`.
Growth attribution uses `jeprof --text --base=t1.sym t2.sym`; the diff represents allocations made between the two dumps that remain live at the later dump.
A growth study should collect t0 immediately after boot, t1 after warmup settles, and t2 after the study window; `--base=t0 t1` attributes warmup and `--base=t1 t2` attributes steady state.

Jemalloc profiler absolute MiB are upper bounds because the profiler allocates its own sampling data, but site rankings remain useful; low-period trace profiling can instead dominate idle diffs through `trace_log` flushing.
The fence-race `/Replacement` test defect was an invalid fixture: it published a `Live` successor catalog row without the successor life’s `_ckpt`; the production fence guarantee remained intact.
The fence-race test must assert the deposed leader fails with `DB::ErrorCodes::NETWORK_ERROR` and a message naming `pre-fold drain lost authority`, rather than accepting any exception.

Every `expectThrowsCode` or `EXPECT_THROW` involving `LOGICAL_ERROR` in `src/Disks/tests/` must be checked against the exact line ranges of `#ifndef DEBUG_OR_SANITIZER_BUILD` guards, not merely file-level guard presence.

CAS gtest suite generation must cross-check source `TEST(...)` discovery with `--gtest_list_tests`, resolve `TEST_P` instantiations, and fail on an unclaimed suite so a silently omitted list cannot appear green.
The final release CA hygiene gate ran 1977 of 1977 tests across 277 suites with 2 disabled and exited 0; the final ASan gate ran 1982 of 1982 tests across 295 suites with 0 sanitizer reports.
The GC bottleneck study measured an approximately 256-log-per-second service rate; its reproduction must sweep arrival rate across that service rate without chaos faults.
The source-edge reducer treats in-degree as a set: an unmatched `-1` must be dropped rather than materialized as a negative edge, because a negative edge could cause a false deletion.
The 56 already-leaked blobs cannot be reclaimed by an incremental round and require a one-off rebuild of in-degree state; this action is separate from a reducer code fix.
In one fold window, 39.6% of manifest fetches were re-reads: 7565 edges came from 4573 distinct manifests, with zero intra-transaction redundancy and cross-transaction add/remove overlap.

The useful manifest-body cache scope is one GC round: an op-scoped or transaction-scoped cache saves nothing, while a round-scoped cache can avoid cross-transaction re-reads; the HEAD-before-GET pair remains vetoed from change.

A mount-time `Cas::Probe` should write a known key set, enumerate it, and refuse LIST-derived discovery on a backend that cannot return the set; the existing `list_consistency_hammer.py` is not this capability probe.
The `gc_anomaly` event must capture a `HEAD` verdict while a LIST/arithmetic disagreement exists, because present and absent are opposite defects and cannot be distinguished reliably after the fact.

The one-shot `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` cap was unsafe: the ref-log cursor could consume an owner-removal entry in the same CAS as a cap-declined cleanup, making the manifest permanently unreachable; durable retry is required before bounding this work.

The CA storage layer can be modeled as a generic VFS of named mutable roots, immutable subtrees, immutable blobs, and mutable overlays; MergeTree-specific part semantics should remain in a thin adapter.

Raw object-storage paths are not a meaningful CAS filesystem interface: logical navigation from a part/ref to tree entries and blob content requires decoding manifests and trees; introspection must provide decoded views.
Concurrent FETCH fan-out can tear the shared `detached` ref on `LocalObjectStorage`, because readers race an in-place truncating rewrite; S3 PUTs are atomic and do not have this specific tear.

A CA-aware cross-disk offload should reuse `checksums.txt` `file_hash`, stream directly to `blobs/<H>/0` without local scratch, verify the digest by default, and prefer metadata-only relink for same-pool moves.
A CA `tryCommit` retry can lose staged `writeFile` or `createHardLink` state because the reset `metadata_transaction` has no `operations_to_execute` entry to refill the in-memory staging maps.

A concurrent ref drop during mutable-only commit can throw through `MergeTreeTransaction::afterCommit`, whose `noexcept` boundary calls `std::terminate`; the race needs a recoverable no-op or an earlier detection path.
Mutable and control protobuf objects should use `CasHeader`; streamed blob payloads should keep a binary envelope, and GC data-plane runs should use `RunFile`.

`RunRef::checksum` is serialized but not validated by consumers, while block and footer CRC32C remains the only checked streaming corruption guard; removing CRC32C before enforcing the run checksum would weaken detection.

`GcHeartbeat` is the outlier in CAS format versioning because it has no magic, version, or `CasHeader`; it must either remain explicitly disposable advisory state or adopt the common header convention.
Pre-beta correctness and oracle blockers include `B207` fsck phantom dangling, `RESURRECT-REUPLOAD-ORPHAN`, dangling precommit manifests, `ca_ro` restart handling, and clean shutdown ordering.
The fence-race `/Replacement` fixture's successor `_ckpt` is life-scoped: the predecessor `_ckpt` at incarnation 177 cannot satisfy a successor at incarnation 178.
The highest-value low-risk refactoring pair is centralizing backend token policy and splitting `CasGc.cpp`; both are intended to preserve storage format and external behavior.
`Store::open` should expose explicit create, read-write existing, and read-only existing modes so read-only opening cannot silently create `_pool_meta` or roots.

If a backend advertises `supportsListTokens`, every listed item should provide a token compatible with `deleteExact` and matching `head`; otherwise the capability must distinguish no tokens from head-only tokens.
GC, orphan sweep, and fsck should share a structured deletion outcome vocabulary: deleted, missing, token mismatch, unsupported, and failed.

CAS introspection should expose pool format and backend capabilities, namespace roots and generations, manifest lifecycle counts, blob reachability, GC cursors, decoded key/object explanations, and machine-readable dry-run reports.

Retired entries can ride the source-edge snapshot as condemned-sentinel rows, reducing the GC merge from three cursors to two; a separate incremental LSM snapshot is an independent later optimization.
The CA soak Python dependencies are `clickhouse-connect>=0.7`, `boto3>=1.34`, and `pytest>=8.0`.

`RunFileReader::next()` can read past a block when an unchecksummed `rec_count` is inflated; the fix must cover the whole block header with CRC and use bounds-checked reads with exact-consumption validation.

An uncaught `CORRUPTED_DATA` from `resolveByExactGet` or `putIfAbsentControlled` in `flushRefBatch` can leave `leader_active` set and waiters blocked indefinitely; the remaining queue must be completed with the exception and notified.
CAS startup capability probing can abort `DiskSelector::initialize()` for unrelated disks because the probe bypasses `skip_access_check` and per-disk startup failures are not isolated.
For an Ordinary database, detached part paths can be parsed into a sibling namespace instead of the table namespace, leaving refs and blobs that `DROP TABLE` never cleans up.

`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC RUN` creates a fresh `Cas::Gc` and is unsynchronized with the background loop, so repeated manual calls cannot accumulate lease-steal observations and may run duplicate leaders.
`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD FORCE` without an explicit disk can bypass healthy-state guards on every CA disk, and routine GC access is currently coupled to the force-rebuild access type.
The `CasGcIsLeader` and `CasGcPendingReclaimEntries` `CurrentMetrics` gauges are process-global rather than per disk, so one CA disk can hide another disk's stuck GC.

The `EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE` precommit requirement must be a release-time check rather than only `chassert(precommitted)`, because `chassert` is compiled out and an early adopt can create a dangle or data loss.

High-risk untested surfaces include the `Mode::Native` object-storage contract, direct CA `DiskObjectStorageTransaction` dispatch ordering, and real-thread races for ref lanes, GC lease stealing, and `Store` teardown.

The proposed root-shard journal controls are `max_unprocedded_journal_records_to_throw` for a hard write-failing limit and `max_unprocedded_journal_records_to_delay` for delaying writes when the journal is long.
A pool-format policy should fail closed at mount for a newer `pool_format_version`, keep immutable blob/tree/envelope formats non-migratable, and state explicitly that downgrade is unsupported.

Format compatibility should guarantee that a new reader can read old object versions, while attempting to read an unknown newer version should fail safely; the proposed `max_content_adressable_pool_format` selects the write-version bundle while headers identify the read version.
The mixed-version rollout design needs cleanup of stale or disappeared server declarations before a pool can advance its common write format.
The `B92` adopt path must populate the correct `tree_size` instead of leaving it at zero.
The format-freeze work for `B176` must review envelope TLV fields and make the streamed `gc/snap` codec preserve streaming, compression, and ordering semantics.
